item.text: {"case_id":"SPR00455","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C07","C02","C17"],"selected_candidate_label":"C07","confidence":0.84,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C07 plausibly supplied a concrete rhetorical and structural template for the child: both letters urge the sitting Congress to act before adjournment, invoke a World War II program or authority as the model, explain why the revived measure is urgently needed for the current defense effort, and distinguish immediate legislation from matters that can await fuller consideration by the next Congress. C02 shares the child's reorganization subject and adjustment-of-government rationale, while C17 supplies closely related mobilization machinery, but neither matches the child's legislative-request architecture as closely as C07.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Two of the measures which we know will be needed are of such importance for the tasks immediately ahead, that I wish to request action by the present Congress before adjournment.","parent_excerpt":"I wish to recommend action in the present session to renew the program of vocational rehabilitation for disabled veterans, which was in effect during and after World War II. ... renewal of these benefits has become a matter of urgency, warranting action before the present Congress adjourns.","explanation":"Both frame an urgent request for action by the present Congress before adjournment."},{"child_excerpt":"The first of these is legislation along the general lines of Title I of the First War Powers Act, 1941 ... available to the President during World War II.","parent_excerpt":"I wish to recommend ... renew[ing] the program ... which was in effect during and after World War II.","explanation":"Both propose reviving or adapting a World War II measure to meet the current conflict's needs."},{"child_excerpt":"As was the case in World War II, these powers will not be used to make permanent changes ... The changes ... will be temporary in nature, for the purpose of furthering the defense effort.","parent_excerpt":"The next Congress will have an opportunity to give full consideration to their longer range needs ... Meanwhile, however, there is no reason for delay in meeting the immediate needs","explanation":"Both separate a narrowly urgent, temporary or immediate measure from longer-range policy that can receive later consideration."}]}
